events.promise: Resend gives the engineer a way to send app-triggered email and test an API event before routing live messages through it.
events.arc: The single email announces Resend’s availability, connects it to the reader’s product-email responsibility, then asks for one contained test.

emails.job: Get a prospective developer to start evaluating Resend with one transactional email event.
emails.single_idea: Resend is available for event-driven transactional email; the reader can start by simulating one API event in test mode before deciding whether to route live product email through it.
emails.objection: Can I evaluate the API without sending real email to users?
must_not_say: Do not claim Resend or a new feature launched today; the platform launched in 2023.
Do not present a Supabase integration as relevant to every recipient.
Do not claim an API test validates an SMTP route or production delivery.
Do not promise to fix upstream Auth configuration changes or another platform’s rate-limit accounting.
Do not add the full integration list, plan comparison, dedicated IPs, security claims, or customer testimonials.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

Only the paid tiers remove the daily cap; on the free plan the engineer swaps one 100/day ceiling for another, and nothing in the ledger speaks to the auth platform's own rate-limit setting that still has to be raised.
emails.felt_need: Auth email sending (signup confirmation, OTP, magic link, invites) gets blocked with a 429 email rate limit error under normal usage, even when the reporter believes they are under the documented limit.
emails.status_quo: Checks the platform's own Auth logs in the dashboard to verify whether the documented email limit was actually exceeded.
emails.mechanism: Resend supports event-driven transactional sending through developer integrations. Its test mode simulates API events without sending real email to real people.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Resend’s API path fits one of the team’s transactional email events.
emails.next_step_value: Create an account and use test mode to simulate an API event without sending real email to real people.
emails.next_step_limit: An API simulation does not verify SMTP integration, live delivery, or another platform’s rate-limit settings.

events.body:
Resend is available for app-triggered transactional email.

Start with one signup confirmation or password-reset event in test mode before deciding whether to route live messages through it. The API event is simulated without sending email to real people.

If an auth flow returns a 429, checking the current platform’s logs can help identify what happened on that route. It cannot tell you whether a separate sending API fits the event your application needs to handle.

Simulate one event to assess Resend’s API. That test does not verify an SMTP connection, live delivery, or the auth platform’s rate-limit settings. It gives you a specific first step before you decide whether to integrate a new sending path.

events.body:
Start with one simulated API event.

Resend is available as an email sending platform for developers. It supports transactional messages triggered by product events, including signup confirmations and password resets. You can evaluate that sending path before routing live product email through it.

In test mode, you can simulate an event without sending email to real people. Use one signup or password-reset event to judge whether Resend’s API path fits how your application triggers messages.

The simulation checks the API path. SMTP integration, live delivery, and rate-limit settings in another platform require separate checks.
